title: First Contact Velocity and Onboard Bundle Playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a compact 'first-contact velocity' + onboarding bundle designed for small-to-medium IC hires where we need speed without sacrificing baseline signals of fit. The goal is to reduce time-to-offer while preserving evidence quality and making the new hire's first week low-friction (quiet launch).

Scope and when to use this bundle
- Use for non-manager IC hires (IC1-IC3) and contractor-to-perm trials where role ramp path is predictable.
- Not recommended for senior IC (staff+) or sensitive regulatory roles (security/compliance exceptions).
- If recruiter signals > 80% match (resume + screen), this bundle shortens interview windows to 5–10 calendar days.

High-level metrics we care about
- First-contact velocity: % of candidates who receive first recruiter outreach response within 24h. Target: 90%
- Time-to-offer: median target 9 days from initial application to written offer for bundle-eligible roles
- Quality signal: pass-rate of hiring manager trial assignment >= 70%
- Quiet-launch friction score (post-week-1 survey): target >= 4/5

Roles & responsibilities
- Recruiter: owns first-contact cadence, scheduling, offer logistics, candidate experience notes
- People Ops (onboarding SWAT): prepares first-week access, welcome doc, laptop checklist, and buddy assignment
- Hiring manager: owns technical probe, short feedback windows (24–48h), first-week onboarding tasks and 1:1 schedule
- Interviewer panel: delivers rubric-aligned feedback within 24h of interview

Pre-screen rubric (explicit, single-page)
- Communication: clear written and spoken explanations of prior projects (0–3)
- Problem decomposition: identifies constraints and tradeoffs (0–3)
- Alignment to role-critical skills: their top two skills map to role needs (0–3)
- Cultural signals: evidence of collaboration and feedback loops (0–2)
- Logistics: right-to-work, location constraints, notice period (pass/fail)
Scores: 8+ pass, 6–7 borderline (manager discretion), <=5 reject.

Interview funnel (condensed)
1) Recruiter screen (30 min) — hire/clear-green filter: logistics + top-level role fit + candidate questions.
2) Manager technical deep-dive (45 min) — focused on 1–2 prior projects and one live whiteboard-style walkthrough (no long coding test).
3) Lightweight take-home trial (optional 48–72h, <=4 hours) — templates exist for frontend/backend/data infra probes.
4) Cross-functional hit (30 min) — convo with a potential peer to validate collaboration rhythm.
5) Offer check-in (15 min) — hiring manager + recruiter sync with candidate to close open rings.

Interview rubric guidance (for interviewers)
- Use the pre-screen rubric numbers, but convert to short bullets in Slack summary (3 lines): 1) strengths, 2) risk/unknowns, 3) recommend (yes/no/hold).
- Mandatory: no later than 24h submit structured feedback. If feedback is late, recruiter flags and arranges a 15-min calibration call.

Sample manager scorecard template (one line per candidate)
- Candidate name | Role match (0–3) | Tech depth (0–3) | Communication (0–3) | Collaboration (0–2) | Recruiter-pulse (pass/fail) | Final rec (yes/hold/no)

Take-home trial suggestions (keep it small)
- Keep trials to 3–4 hours of real work. Provide clear acceptance criteria and sample solution outline. Trials are optional: if manager strongly prefers live interview, skip trial.

Offer & compensation checklist (Recruiter)
- Confirm comp band for the role and manager sign-off
- Draft written offer with clear start date window, equity outline (if any), and relocation/remote policy
- Pre-share first-week agenda so candidate knows day-one expectations

Onboarding: Quiet Launch (first 7 days)
Principles: minimize churn (less meetings), maximize essentials (access, context, buddy).
Day 0 (prestart)
- Laptop issued and imaged, account invites sent (Slack, Google, Github, infra VPN).
- Welcome doc sent: 1 paragraph about team mission, 3 priorities for 90 days, buddy intro.

Day 1
- 30-min manager welcome (low-level mission + 1:1 cadence)
- 30-min buddy orientation (how to find code, test locally, first ticket)
- Access validation: confirm dev environment + repo clone + CI run within day 1
- No more than 2 initial deep meetings scheduled

Day 2–3
- First small ticket assigned (≤ 8 hours) with mentor pairing for onboarding
- Security/HR short forms completed asynchronously (no >30min synchronous sessions)

Day 4–5
- Project context session with product/PM (45 min)
- Team async review of first ticket; manager gives feedback within 24h

End of Week 1
- 30-min manager check-in + 30-min buddy retro: rate friction and progress
- New hire pulse (quick form): friction score 1–5 and blockers list

Manager onboarding checklist (first 14 days)
- Confirm workstream and 3-month outcomes with new hire in writing
- Assign clear owner for first ticket and rotate mentor responsibility every 2 weeks
- Schedule recurring 1:1s and a 30-min weekly sync for the first month
- Provide 3 short reading items (design docs, architecture notes) to be consumed in week 1

Exit criteria and early risk signals (for people ops)
- Exit criteria to escalate: new hire friction score <= 2 on week 1 pulse OR failure to get dev env working by Day 2 -> escalate to People Ops within 24h.
- Risk signals: repeated meeting overload, unclear ownership of first task, lagging feedback from manager (over 72h).

Templates + quick copy (to paste)
- Recruiter outreach subject: "Quick chat about the [ROLE] at Redwood Inference — 15 min?"
- Day 0 welcome (one-paragraph): "Welcome to Redwood — excited to have you join [team]. Your first week will be a quiet launch: focused setup, one small ticket, and buddy support. Your buddy is [NAME] — they'll ping you on Slack at 9am PST on Day 1. If anything blocks you before Day 1, reply to this thread and we’ll help."

Open questions / decisions
- Do we permit 'live coding only' for roles that historically have used take-homes? (tradeoff: speed vs observable work product)
- Should relocation offers be handled as separate negotiation flows or bundled into the written offer in all cases?
- Auto-assigning buddies: can we ship a small internal tool to randomly rotate buddy assignment? (linked PR above)

Notes to self
- We should pilot this bundle in hiring for infra-engineer IC2 in April. Track a 10-person cohort and compare to baseline time-to-offer and 90-day performance signals.
- Keep the trial templates in the onboarding repo small; avoid problem sets that more closely resemble full take-home tasks for senior hires.

References
- See linked Confluence playbook for longer policy notes and comp band matrix.
- Slack channel to watch: #people-ops-hiring and #onboard-swat.

End of doc.
